original_card.question: Can an explicitly larger or nonabelian register model escape the scoped three-register obstruction?
methods: Construct the smallest exact identity in a newly specified legal operation alphabet.
Derive a target-specific relaxation bound for that same explicit alphabet.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Name the changed hypothesis, all counted roles and a uniform identity; finite column tests alone do not certify it. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: First compare the alphabet, role count and length with the fully replayed #1974 census and #2027 mixed-root tariff. Identify a changed premise and a legal native implementation; then price one smallest completed instance before searching larger words.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A small-width completed saving changes the bit primitive; a finite-address identity alone is insufficient.
allowed_variations: Choose a fixed larger register count or a specified nonabelian operation family.
scope_change_triggers: Remaining inside the already-excluded three-register abelian model.
Repeating the two-register GL3 census or a covered three-register length without changing a hypothesis; a formal group-algebra word without native conversion is a partial result.

actual_scope: Whether every complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension at most 4 whose covectors all have weight 1 has joint-image dimension at most 6, and is reducible once that dimension exceeds the pattern dimension.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a larger or nonabelian register alphabet. This package answers the weight-1 case of the pattern-dimension-4 irreducible-image question left by #6962 and narrowed by open #7094. No new alphabet, word, or kappa is claimed. The same card was already moved to scalar pattern-pool questions by #5921, #6838, #6921 and #6962.
bottleneck_link: Side result. A later word argument cannot quote an irreducible image of dimension 5 or 6 for a weight-1 no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4. The original native acceptance gate remains unmet, and the selected frontier is unchanged.
stop_rule: Stop once the weight-1 bound and the dimension-6 witness are proved, including the kernel test and the partition table. Do not search heavy covectors or claim they are impossible.
evidence: PROOF.md proves dim V <= 6 and reducibility when dim V >= dim P + 1, for no-edge pools of pattern dimension at most 4 whose covectors all have weight 1. verify.py exhaustively enumerates the width-8 witness (pool 6, image 6, kernel 4), the one-column image of dimension 5, the four-line example with trivial kernel, and the negative controls.
author: unpaidmoon
ai_assistance: Substantial Cursor Grok assistance with the column decomposition, the witness, and the package verifier. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a complete no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 that uses at least one covector of weight 2 or more act irreducibly on a joint image of dimension 6 or more?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Open #7094 gives irreducible dimension 5 with heavy covectors, so the weight-1 cap of 6 does not bound that class. An irreducible dimension-6 example, or a proof that none exists, is the question #6962 left after the dimension-5 witness.
open_questions.first_step: Give one explicit heavy-covector pool with a written invariant-subspace check, or prove that every such pool has image dimension at most 5 or is reducible.
open_questions.blocked_by: The weight-1 column decomposition does not apply, and no support reduction in this package makes the heavy-covector domain finite. A search that finds nothing would not be a proof.

open_questions.question: Is every weight-1 no-edge pool of pattern dimension 4 with joint-image dimension 4 reducible?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The kernel test needs dim V >= dim P + 1. The four disjoint lines have dim V = 4, trivial common kernel, and are reducible by another invariant subspace, so they do not settle the general dim-4 case.
open_questions.first_step: Either exhibit a weight-1 pattern-dimension-4 pool whose four-dimensional image has no proper nonzero invariant subspace, or prove that every such action has one.
open_questions.blocked_by: The common-kernel count can be zero, so that test does not finish the argument.
